questions.question: When driving under a bridge or overpass, you should:

options.text: Trust that the posted clearance height is correct.
Do not assume the posted clearance height is correct.
Measure the opening height before driving through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the posted clearance height is correct.
questions.explanation: Do not trust posted height clearances. The road may have been repaved after the sign was posted. Snow on the ground can also change the actual height. If you are not sure your vehicle will fit safely, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Backing a large vehicle is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both side mirrors often while backing. Use a helper whenever you can.

questions.question: Most bus accidents happen:
questions.explanation: Most bus accidents occur at intersections. Be careful at all intersections, even ones with signs or traffic lights.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It takes your mind and hands off driving.
A message might upset the driver.
People may become too focused on their phone.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your mind and hands off driving.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is very dangerous. It distracts your mind from the road and requires you to remove at least one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: On a bus, carry-on baggage should be stored:

options.text: In a way that lets riders exit through any window or door in an emergency.
In the aisle near the front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a way that lets riders exit through any window or door in an emergency.
questions.explanation: Keep aisles and stairwells clear on a bus. All luggage and freight must be placed so passengers can exit through any window or door in an emergency.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving maneuvers and your overall driving behavior.

questions.question: When should you adjust mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Make sure they are positioned correctly for your comfort and safety.

questions.question: ____ cannot be transported on a bus where people are sitting.
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials labeled as hazardous must never be carried in areas where passengers are present on a bus.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean the nuts are loose. Check how tight the wheel nuts are before you drive.

questions.question: Too much air pressure in a tire:
questions.explanation: Tires should never have too much air pressure. Check your tire pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: A ramp's posted speed limit:

options.text: Works for some vehicles, but may be too fast for large trucks.
Is just a suggestion and can be exceeded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Works for some vehicles, but may be too fast for large trucks.
questions.explanation: Ramp speed limits are set for cars. Large or heavily-loaded trucks may need to go slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: If planning to change lanes, your mirrors should:

options.text: Be checked more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be checked more often than usual.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly as part of normal driving. When changing lanes, check them even more often.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:
questions.explanation: Inspect your vehicle at the end of every trip or shift. Complete a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, you should not:

options.text: Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on while you complete the turn or lane change. Turn off the signal as soon as you finish to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.question: A liver can process about ____ per hour.
questions.explanation: The liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate of about one drink per hour. The faster you drink, the higher your blood alcohol will become.

questions.question: If a truck is equipped, a trailer brake hand valve can be used to:

options.text: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the truck from rolling backward when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: The trailer brake hand valve prevents the vehicle from rolling back when you start moving from a stop.

questions.question: During testing exercises, you may exit your vehicle to check its position up to:
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during most exercises. This is called a "look." You may do one look during straight line backing. You may do two looks during any other exercise.

questions.question: When accelerating on a wet road, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about the road surface.

questions.explanation: Accelerate very slowly on wet roads or other surfaces with poor traction.

questions.question: When checking power steering hoses during a pre-trip inspection, you should look for:
questions.explanation: Check power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level during a pre-trip inspection. Look especially for leaks in the hoses.
